artifacts.summary: 4-phase, ~3.25h plan to add the shared .lake build-guard flock and an environment-failure diagnostic class to scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh, correct its stale CI-wiring header claim, and prove both new paths with negative controls.

memory_candidates.content: An unguarded .lake READER is as exposed as a writer. A repo gate that loops `lake env lean` over files outside the build graph (scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh, 33 probes) can read half-rewritten oleans while a concurrent `lake build` rebuilds the import-closure tail, producing `error: object file '.../FormalSystem/<Module>.olean' of module ... does not exist`. Diagnostic rule: a missing-object-file error is ALWAYS an environment/I/O failure, never source or probe rot -- the measurement never reached the file's own content. Shape signature of the race: consecutive entries failing in one run, each naming a DIFFERENT tail module, with those oleans' mtimes inside the run window. Remedy pattern: take the same exclusive flock on <root>/.lake/build-guard.lock that lake-build-guard.sh publishes and check-module-invariants.sh's C1 block already takes -- once per run, fd held to process exit so later .lake reads inherit it, `flock -n` then a bounded announced `flock -w`, degrading audibly when flock is absent. Corollary for gate authors: a failure vocabulary with only source-level classes forces a conservative reader to mis-attribute a transient environment fault as rot, which is how one race became two Reasoned Exclusions and a repair task.
